LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD is safe to process with `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` and `makepkg --printsrcinfo`. 

The source definition points to a standard tar.gz archive from the official GitHub repository (`https://github.com/shell-pool/shpool/archive/v0.11.3.tar.gz`), which is the expected upstream source for this package. The SHA512 checksum is provided and not marked as SKIP, so there is no integrity concern at this stage. During the audit, the source will be fetched and extracted (standard behavior for AUR packages), but no code execution occurs—only file extraction. The top-level of the PKGBUILD contains only benign variable assignments and string literals; the actual build logic resides in the `build()`, `check()`, and `package()` functions, which are not invoked due to the `--nobuild` and `--noprepare` flags. Therefore, neither command executes genuinely malicious code.
</details>
<evidence></evidence>
<summary>The source is a standard tar.gz from the official GitHub repository with a valid checksum, and the audit commands only fetch/extract without executing any code.</summary>
